root_semantic_findings: Frame dedup owns the key, Arc original and V. K selects a bucket and complete str equality selects an entry; no Unicode normalization, type-wide Ready gate, capacity trimming or automatic frame scheduling is supplied.

begin_frame always clears entries and replaces the report, even for equal or decreasing frame indices. Explicit clear preserves frame/history and increases clear_count. UI owner calls begin_frame; its finish_frame only finishes persistent caches/session.

get/get_or_insert use find_slot and accumulate final hits or misses; a collision miss requires unequal original candidates and final absence. insert contributes candidates and insertion/update only, not read hits/misses.

get_or_insert consumes key and closure ownership; hit does not invoke the closure. Miss owns a new Arc and invokes FnOnce once. Returned V is a cache borrow; independent resources require the caller own/clone them. Index callbacks alter only V and preserve bucket identity; frame paths pass track_lru=false.

Shared cases are a mixed measure/layout/frame/shaped closure. Counter-based fixed-capacity fixtures and Arc pointer equality do not establish allocator behavior, physical constant time, real shaping, or maximum RSS.

Residency fixtures derive update deltas from the first report with equal-length fixed texts. clear asserts only current estimated_bytes zero; peak retention is an implementation-context fact rather than an executed or direct fixture assertion.

Three nonempty-language tests call key/lookup constructors without canonicalized: horizontal/with_language sets language_is_canonical=false; default empty features allow the preceding feature assertion; enabled debug assertions fail first at language. Seven later assertion macros are blocked.

With debug assertions disabled, the first equivalence fixture preserves raw case-variant language strings in derived key equality, making its ordinary equality assertion false. No disabled-debug outcome is inferred for the other two fixtures. No test was executed or behavior changed.
